messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.s@orchidhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrchidHealth production rejections and latency spike

Camila —

We started seeing a large number of 429s and timeouts from your API starting ~08:45 PDT. Throughput dropped and a subset of our high-priority tenant requests are being rejected. Attached are a few request samples and a short trace dump.

This is impacting our scheduling flows (customers delayed). Can you confirm whether this is on your side and whether there is a mitigation you can apply quickly?

We need something in the next 2 hours if possible — escalation started internally.

Thanks,
Priya
VP Product, OrchidHealth
Attachments: orchid-request-samples-090915.json (json), orchid-traces-090915.zip (zip)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya.s@orchidhealth.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrchidHealth production rejections and latency spike

Priya / Sanjay —

Thank you for the samples and the trace. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read shows repeated request rejections that line up with our burst-safety window tripping for your tenant. I don't see an application-level error on our side yet — the traces look like enforcement at the request-shaper layer (429 / rate-limiter).

Immediate actions I will take now:
- Open an ops incident and route to SRE and Runtime (tracking: SUP-3219).
- Request a temporary burst-window override for OrchidHealth while we investigate.
- Ask you to confirm if any traffic pattern change happened on your side (bulk retries, large batched jobs).

Can you confirm whether you pushed any job around 08:30–08:50 PDT? If not, I will proceed with a timeboxed override and loop in execs for visibility.

I'll follow up within 20–30 minutes with the ops incident link and a mitigation plan.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: OrchidHealth production rejections and latency spike — urgent ops + exec visibility

Folks — forwarding customer thread. OrchidHealth (large paying account, scheduling product) reports widespread 429s and latency spikes starting ~08:45 PDT. Attached traces (orchid-traces-090915.zip) show enforcement at the request-shaper.

Why I need help ASAP:
- Customer is blocked; internal escalation at their end.
- Our quick hypothesis: a mismatch between the tenant quota window (per-minute commitments) and the burst safety valve. Effect: sustained burst inside a short timeslice causes safety valve to trip and drop legitimate requests, causing retries and escalating load.

What I propose for immediate mitigation (please action now):
1) Approve a temporary bump of Orchids' burst allowance and extend the burst window from 5s to 15s (timeboxed 2 hours). This should allow the queued requests to drain.
2) Enable soft-fail fallback to the next-compatible model variant for requests currently failing due to rate-limit enforcement (route CPU to less expensive variant).
3) Create an ops ticket (SUP-3219) and kick off an RCA focusing on: burst-window config, token-bucket leak detection, and routing policy that may be double-counting nested requests.

Evidence from quick trace read: repeated 429s show X-RateLimit-Remaining hits 0 then sudden drop; a lot of identical retry bursts within 10s. That smells like safety valve window too small combined with aggressive retrybackoffs from the client.

Customer impact/ask: temporary override + continuous monitoring. If we can't provide a fix in 2 hours, they will request credit and exec involvement.

I can join any quick bridge. Please reply with "ACK + action" and the change you will make.

—Camila

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrchidHealth production rejections and latency spike — urgent ops + exec visibility

ACK + action.

Thanks for the signal and the diagnostic Camila. We will take the following path immediately:
- Temporary mitigation: Ops will apply a 2‑hour burst-window extension for OrchidHealth at 16:30 PDT today (change id: CHG-6652). This is limited scope and monitored.
- Soft fallback: Runtime team will enable fallback routing to the compatible to-CPU variant for the tenant for 2 hours to reduce pressure on the fast path.
- Monitoring: SRE will add a trace-level watch and alerting for rising retry loops for SUP-3219.

Next steps and commitments:
1) RCA will be produced by 2026-09-20 EOD. Focus areas: token-bucket math in multi-tenant path, burst-window value sensitivity, and any recent policy rollout that may have changed enforcement thresholds.
2) Post-mortem and recommended config changes presented to Execs (you, Vivek, and Growth) by 2026-09-21.
3) If RCA shows config drift or a control-plane bug, we will follow through with a global fix and backfill for affected tenants.

Camila — please send me the internal ops link and customer contact info. Camila / Vivek: loop in Sales Ops if the customer requests credits; keep me posted on tone.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
